display_title: Fix DCE and VJP tangent effects for Ref mutations in jax_remat3.

head_commit.message:
Fix DCE and VJP tangent effects for Ref mutations in jax_remat3.

When a `RematTraced` or other `HiPrim` mutates an input or closed-over `Ref` whose return value is unused in the differentiated output (e.g. `z` is in `has_aux=True` or `nz_out_flat` is empty), `fake_linear_op` previously early-returned `Zero`s and `call_hi_primitive_linearized_p` was defined without effects, causing `tangent_trace` and `_call_hi_primitive_linearized_dce` to eliminate the equation and drop the `Ref` gradient.

- In `hijax.py`, map `prim.effects` onto the nonzero tangent inputs via `_linearized_effects`, check `has_tangent_effects` before early-returning in `fake_linear_op`, and register `call_hi_primitive_linearized_p` with `is_effectful` and `@call_hi_primitive_linearized_p.def_effectful_abstract_eval`.
- In `ad_checkpoint.py`, pass `live_inputs=False` to `pe.dce_jaxpr` in `dce()` so primal `Ref` writes in `make_vjp`/`make_lin` are not treated as live outputs, avoiding saving internal/frozen `Ref`s in `primals_` under `@jax.jit`.
- In `ad_checkpoint.py`, check `arg_accums` in `RematTraced.vjp_bwd` so zero functional cotangents (`outgrad`) do not discard backward `RefAccum` cotangents.
- In `hijax_test.py`, add unit tests in `CustomVJPRemat3Test` verifying gradient and VJP calculation for eager and jit-compiled functions where rematted blocks mutate a `Ref` with auxiliary return values or no return values.

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Fix jax.scipy.special.expi(+inf) returning NaN (jax-ml/jax#38519)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#38519 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38519), `jax.scipy.special.expi(np.inf)` returns `NaN` instead of `inf` because `_expi_pos` has no condition for `+inf` and falls through to `_expint7`, which evaluates `exp(inf) * (1 / inf)`. In addition, because `jnp.piecewise` evaluates all branch functions before selecting, out-of-domain values in unselected branches (`_expint1`, `_eval_expint_k`, and `_expi_neg`) produce unselected `NaN`s under `jax.debug_nans(True)`.

Solution:
Add an explicit `jnp.isposinf(x)` condition returning `np.inf` in `_expi_pos`, sanitize out-of-domain inputs in `_expint1`, `_eval_expint_k`, and `_expi_neg` for `jax.debug_nans(True)` safety, and add a regression test `testExpiInf` in `lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38519

display_title: [Pallas:MGPU] Consolidate TMEM transpose and reshape checks into lowe…

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:MGPU] Consolidate TMEM transpose and reshape checks into lowering.

`plgpu.transpose_ref` is being deprecated in favor of `ref.transpose` / `ref.T`, and its eager `ref.memory_space` check both fails on untransformed `Ref` tracers (since `Tracer.memory_space` is disallowed) and is bypassed when calling `ref.transpose` directly.

Delegate `plgpu.transpose_ref` directly to `ref.transpose(permutation)`, and check `ref_aval.memory_space == gpu_core.TMEM` in `_handle_transforms` so that TMEM transpose and reshape checks apply to `ref.transpose` / `ref.reshape` across both `Lane` and `Warpgroup` lowering semantics.

display_title: Synchronize remote TMA output in dynamic peer DMA test

head_commit.message:
Synchronize remote TMA output in dynamic peer DMA test

In multiprocess runs, `test_remote_dma_dynamic_other_device_id` allocates
`kernel`'s output `y` in collective symmetric memory (`S(7)`), causing XLA:GPU
to append a local-stream `S(7)` to `S(0)` copy of the module output. Because
`MosaicGpuExecute` only runs a pre-kernel multi-GPU barrier and
`wait_smem_to_gmem(0)` only waits for the local outgoing TMA store, each GPU's
output copy raced against the peer GPU's incoming TMA write into `y`. The
kernel also omitted `commit_smem()` between the shared-memory store and
`copy_smem_to_gmem`.

Add `plgpu.commit_smem()` before `copy_smem_to_gmem`, and synchronize across
devices in a follow-up `sync_kernel` that signals and waits on a semaphore
before copying `y_ref` to a new output `z_ref`. Keeping cross-device semaphore
signaling in `sync_kernel` avoids calling `launch_ctx.to_remote` while lowering
`kernel`, preserving Warpgroup `device_collective_metadata` DCE regression
coverage, while returning `z_ref` orders XLA's `S(7)` to `S(0)` output copy
after the peer TMA write completes.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Synchronize remote TMA output in dynamic peer DMA test

head_commit.message:
Synchronize remote TMA output in dynamic peer DMA test

In multiprocess runs, `test_remote_dma_dynamic_other_device_id` allocates
`kernel`'s output `y` in collective symmetric memory (`S(7)`), causing XLA:GPU
to append a local-stream `S(7)` to `S(0)` copy of the module output. Because
`MosaicGpuExecute` only runs a pre-kernel multi-GPU barrier and
`wait_smem_to_gmem(0)` only waits for the local outgoing TMA store, each GPU's
output copy raced against the peer GPU's incoming TMA write into `y`. The
kernel also omitted `commit_smem()` between the shared-memory store and
`copy_smem_to_gmem`.

Add `plgpu.commit_smem()` before `copy_smem_to_gmem`, and synchronize across
devices in a follow-up `sync_kernel` that signals and waits on a semaphore
before copying `y_ref` to a new output `z_ref`. Keeping cross-device semaphore
signaling in `sync_kernel` avoids calling `launch_ctx.to_remote` while lowering
`kernel`, preserving Warpgroup `device_collective_metadata` DCE regression
coverage, while returning `z_ref` orders XLA's `S(7)` to `S(0)` output copy
after the peer TMA write completes.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [pallas:fuser] Evaluate unblocked values on unblocked operands.

head_commit.message:
[pallas:fuser] Evaluate unblocked values on unblocked operands.

A value with no block transform holds its full value, and `kernel_fn`
evaluates every equation with a `Usage.REGULAR` output. However,
`_pull_block_transform` skipped equations whose outputs are all unblocked, so
their operands never recorded that they are needed in full. A shared input
could therefore get a block spec from another consumer, and the unblocked
equations were then evaluated on its block with block eval rules: for example,
`x - x[i, 5]` silently computed `x_blk - x_blk == 0` in every block, because
the `dynamic_slice` and `squeeze` eval rules return their operand unchanged.

* `_pull_block_transform` now applies `_unblocked_pull_rule` to evaluated
  equations with unblocked outputs, which records no block transform for their
  operands, and still builds their scalar prefetch function. A conflicting
  blocked use of the same value is then rejected by the existing "Fusion
  contains a DAG" check.
* `kernel_fn` evaluates equations whose outputs are all unblocked with
  `_unblocked_eval_rule`, which binds the primitive on the full operands. It
  replaces `register_default_eval_rule`, used only for `axis_index`.

display_title: Mark the complex exp2 ninfj and pinfj regions as inaccurate in lax_test.

head_commit.message:
Mark the complex exp2 ninfj and pinfj regions as inaccurate in lax_test.

llvm/llvm-project#232791 changed MLIR's ComplexToStandard lowering of
complex.exp, which XLA CPU and GPU use, to return the C99 Annex G values when
the real part is infinite and the imaginary part is not finite. As a result
exp2(-inf - inf*j) is now 0j and exp2(inf - inf*j) is inf + nanj, while the
mpmath reference used by testSuccessOnComplexPlane gives nan + nanj.

The test now treats those regions as known inaccurate for exp2, so it passes
with XLA built against LLVM from before or after that change.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Improve accuracy of real gamma and factorial.

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy of real gamma and factorial.

Real `jax.scipy.special.gamma` previously used a single-word Lanczos approximation (~10 ULP error on CPU/GPU and ~300 ULP on TPU), and `jax.scipy.special.factorial` evaluated `exp(lgamma(n + 1))`, losing precision on larger integers.

Implement real `gamma` in `jax._src.scipy.gamma` using `(hi, lo)` double-word arithmetic with shared `exp_f2_mant_exp` and `scale_f2_pow2` helpers in `jax._src.lax.double_word`, and route `factorial(n)` through `gamma(n + 1)`. Real `gamma` now stays within 0.5 ULP for `bfloat16` and 1.0 ULP for `float16`, `float32`, and `float64` across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and returns exact factorials up to 34! in `float32` and 170! in `float64`.

display_title: Fix hyp1f1 values and gradients for negative x

head_commit.message:
Stop the hyp1f1 series where it terminates, and speed up its tests

The series loop kept running after a vanishing term while
k <= |x| - min(b, 0), which gave NaN once b + k reached 0 for a
negative integer b (e.g. hyp1f1(-1., -3., 5.)). The convergence checks
now multiply by eps instead of dividing by the sum, so they no longer
see 0 / 0 when exp(x / 2) underflows.

In the numerics tests, the ignore predicates only evaluate the
reference on the samples within the tested domain, run the asymptotic
convergence loop only where it is used, and reuse the series sums for
the cancellation estimate. The x-derivative evaluates the reference
once. The gradient tests are split into one class each and run on four
shards.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [JAX] Fix jax.scipy.special.betaln for negative integers, zero, and infinite inputs (jax-ml/jax#38243, jax-ml/jax#39106)

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Fix jax.scipy.special.betaln for negative integers, zero, and infinite inputs (jax-ml/jax#38243, jax-ml/jax#39106)

Problem:
1. In jax-ml/jax#38243 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38243), `jax.scipy.special.betaln(a, b)` returns `NaN` when one argument is a negative integer `-n` and the other is a positive integer `b <= n`, because `lax.lgamma(new_a)` and `lax.lgamma(new_a + new_b)` both evaluate to `inf` at non-positive integer poles and cancel as `inf - inf`. In addition, when `new_a < 0` and `new_b >= 8` without integer reflection such that `new_a + new_b < 8`, `betaln` routed to `algdiv`, where `a / b <= -1` yields `NaN` in `lax.log1p(a / b)` or inaccurate Stirling series values, and `algdiv` had a pre-existing `x = h / (1 + h)` typo instead of `x = 1.0 / (1.0 + h)`.
2. In jax-ml/jax#39106 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39106), `jax.scipy.special.betaln` returns `NaN` on infinite and zero boundary arguments (and fails under `jax.debug_nans(True)`):
   - In `algdiv(a, b)`, when `b` is infinite, `u = d * lax.log1p(a / b)` evaluates `inf * 0 = NaN` and `v = a * (lax.log(b) - 1.0)` evaluates `0 * inf = NaN` when `a == 0`.
   - In `betaln(a, b)`, because `jnp.where` evaluates both branches, the unselected `small_b` branch evaluates `lgamma(inf) - lgamma(a + inf) = inf - inf = NaN` when `b = inf` (and `lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b) = inf - inf = NaN` when both `a` and `b` are non-positive integers), while the unselected `large_b` branch evaluates `algdiv(0, 0)` (`0 / 0 = NaN`) when `b < 8`.

Solution:
1. Apply the beta reflection identity `betaln(a, b) = betaln(1 - a - b, b)` when `new_a` is a finite negative integer, `new_b` is a finite positive integer, and `new_a <= -new_b`, re-sorting the reflected pair with `jnp.where(reflected_a <= new_b, ...)` so `new_a <= new_b` holds and gradients at `reflected_a == new_b` remain consistent.
2. Route both `new_b < 8` and `new_a + new_b < 8` (`(new_b < 8) | (new_a < 8 - new_b)`) to `small_b`, and fix `x = 1.0 / (1.0 + h)` in `algdiv` per `cdflib/algdiv.f`.
3. In `algdiv`, replace `u` with its asymptotic limit `a` when `b` is infinite (masking `d_safe = jnp.where(b_is_inf, 0.0, d)` in the false branch) and guard `v` when `b_is_inf & (a == 0.0)` (masking `a_safe = jnp.where(b_is_inf & (a == 0.0), 1.0, a)` in the false branch so gradients at `a = 0` are preserved for finite `b`).
4. In `betaln`, mask the inputs to `(lgamma(b) - lgamma(a + b))` in `small_b` unless `is_small_b & ~(is_nonpos_int_a & is_nonpos_int_b)` and mask the inputs to `algdiv` in `large_b` when `is_small_b`, avoiding unselected `NaN`s under `jax.debug_nans(True)` and returning `+inf` when both inputs are non-positive integers or one is `0.0`.
5. Add regression tests `testBetalnNegativeIntegers` and `testBetalnInf` in `lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38243
Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39106

[JAX] Fix state discharge of get, swap, and addupdate on pinned refs (jax-ml/jax#41846)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#41846 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41846), reading, updating, or add-updating a reference created with `jax.ref.new_ref(x, pin=True)` fails with `ValueError: Attempting to pass an unexpected type AbstractLinVal` because `_get_discharge_rule`, `_swap_discharge_rule`, and `_addupdate_discharge_rule` in `jax/_src/state/discharge.py` do not unpin `AbstractLinVal` tracers before applying operations or re-pin the updated state afterward.

Solution:
Unpin `AbstractLinVal` inputs in `_get_discharge_rule`, `_swap_discharge_rule`, and `_addupdate_discharge_rule` and re-pin the resulting state with its original `memory_space`, preserving the linear chain. Add a regression test in `tests/state_test.py`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/41846

display_title: [JAX] Avoid intermediate exp overflow in i0 and i1 for large finite i…

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Avoid intermediate exp overflow in i0 and i1 for large finite inputs (jax-ml/jax#39770, jax-ml/jax#39772)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#39770 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39770) and jax-ml/jax#39772 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39772), jax.numpy.i0, jax.scipy.special.i0, and jax.scipy.special.i1 evaluate exp(|x|) * bessel_i0e(|x|) (or bessel_i1e(x)), which overflows the intermediate exp(|x|) to inf when |x| exceeds 709.78 in float64 (88.72 in float32) even when the unscaled Bessel result fits within the finite floating-point range (up to |x| ~ 713.98 in float64 and |x| ~ 91.9 in float32).

Solution:
1. Extract _exp_mul_bessel_ie(abs_x, ie) for _i1 and i0_impl: when |x| is at most floor(log(finfo(dtype).max)), evaluate ie * exp(|x|) so low-precision dtypes (e.g. bfloat16) do not accumulate extra rounding error from squaring exp(|x|/2); when |x| exceeds max_log, split the exponent as (exp(|x|/2) * ie) * exp(|x|/2) while still issuing only a single lax.exp op per call.
2. In i1_impl_jvp, use the closed-form Bessel recurrence i0_impl(x) - i1_impl(x) / x when |x| exceeds sqrt(eps) (while keeping _i1_maclaurin(1, x) near zero) so higher-order reverse-mode AD (e.g. jax.grad(jax.grad(i1))) differentiates through i0_impl and i1_impl custom JVPs rather than transposing half_exp * i1e * half_exp.
3. Add test_i0_i1_large_inputs in lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py covering values, 1st- and 2nd-order gradients, JIT compilation, and true overflow in float32 and float64.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39770
Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39772

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Avoid intermediate exp overflow in i0 and i1 for large finite inputs (jax-ml/jax#39770, jax-ml/jax#39772)

Problem:
In jax-ml/jax#39770 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39770) and jax-ml/jax#39772 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39772), jax.numpy.i0, jax.scipy.special.i0, and jax.scipy.special.i1 evaluate exp(|x|) * bessel_i0e(|x|) (or bessel_i1e(x)), which overflows the intermediate exp(|x|) to inf when |x| exceeds 709.78 in float64 (88.72 in float32) even when the unscaled Bessel result fits within the finite floating-point range (up to |x| ~ 713.98 in float64 and |x| ~ 91.9 in float32).

1. Extract _exp_mul_bessel_ie(abs_x, ie) for _i1 and i0_impl: when |x| is at most floor(log(finfo(dtype).max)), evaluate ie * exp(|x|) so low-precision dtypes (e.g. bfloat16) do not accumulate extra rounding error from squaring exp(|x|/2); when |x| exceeds max_log, split the exponent as (exp(|x|/2) * ie) * exp(|x|/2) while still issuing only a single lax.exp op per call.

display_title: [hijax] Use FlatTrees in CustomJVPTraced/CustomVJPTraced

head_commit.message:
[hijax] Use FlatTrees in CustomJVPTraced/CustomVJPTraced

Under custom_jvp3/custom_vjp3, user pytree nodes were constructed around
non-Array leaves (`ArgInfo`, `ShapedArray`, internal `ad.Zero` tangents and
cotangents, accumulators), breaking pytree classes that validate their leaves
(e.g. TFP's `LinearOperator`). For example, with `jax_custom_vjp3=True`:

```python
@jax.tree_util.register_pytree_node_class
class Node:  # like TFP's LinearOperator, validates its leaves
  def __init__(self, a):
    if not isinstance(a, jax.Array):
      raise TypeError(f"expected a jax.Array, got {type(a).__name__}")
    self.a = a
  def tree_flatten(self):
    return (self.a,), None
  @classmethod
  def tree_unflatten(cls, _, children):
    return cls(*children)

@jax.custom_vjp
def f(node, y):
  return node.a * y
f.defvjp(lambda node, y: (f(node, y), (node, y)),
         lambda res, g: (Node(g * res[1]), g * res[0].a))

jax.grad(f, argnums=1)(Node(jnp.float32(3.)), jnp.float32(4.))
# before: TypeError: expected a jax.Array, got ArgInfo
# after: 3.0
```

`Traced.with_consts_as_arg` now returns a flat `Traced`, taking
`(consts, *args_flat)` and returning a flat list, so that it never rebuilds
argument or result pytrees around avals (it used to unflatten avals into the
user's argument pytrees to re-trace). `CustomJVPTraced`/`CustomVJPTraced` hold
that flat `Traced` and take the user's non-static arguments as flat leaves. The
wrapper closures around the user's rules hold a FlatTree of the arguments
(nondiff arguments as `FTStatic`s, key paths as leaves), and use it and the
original `Traced`'s output tree to rebuild user pytrees only at the rule
boundary, after instantiating (or converting to `SymbolicZero`) any internal
symbolic zeros. Residuals cross the `HiPrim` boundary as
`(leaves, Static(treedef))`.

Validating pytree nodes still can't hold leaves that the user-facing API itself
makes non-Arrays: symbolic zeros under `symbolic_zeros=True` (`SymbolicZero`,
`CustomVJPPrimal`), and accumulators under `defvjp_with_accums`.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules).

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [hijax] Use FlatTrees in CustomJVPTraced/CustomVJPTraced

head_commit.message:
[hijax] Use FlatTrees in CustomJVPTraced/CustomVJPTraced

Under custom_jvp3/custom_vjp3, user pytree nodes were constructed around
non-Array leaves (`ArgInfo`, `ShapedArray`, internal `ad.Zero` tangents and
cotangents, accumulators), breaking pytree classes that validate their leaves
(e.g. TFP's `LinearOperator`). For example, with `jax_custom_vjp3=True`:

```python
@jax.tree_util.register_pytree_node_class
class Node:  # like TFP's LinearOperator, validates its leaves
  def __init__(self, a):
    if not isinstance(a, jax.Array):
      raise TypeError(f"expected a jax.Array, got {type(a).__name__}")
    self.a = a
  def tree_flatten(self):
    return (self.a,), None
  @classmethod
  def tree_unflatten(cls, _, children):
    return cls(*children)

@jax.custom_vjp
def f(node, y):
  return node.a * y
f.defvjp(lambda node, y: (f(node, y), (node, y)),
         lambda res, g: (Node(g * res[1]), g * res[0].a))

jax.grad(f, argnums=1)(Node(jnp.float32(3.)), jnp.float32(4.))
# before: TypeError: expected a jax.Array, got ArgInfo
# after: 3.0
```

`Traced.with_consts_as_arg` now returns a flat `Traced`, taking
`(consts, *args_flat)` and returning a flat list, so that it never rebuilds
argument or result pytrees around avals (it used to unflatten avals into the
user's argument pytrees to re-trace). `CustomJVPTraced`/`CustomVJPTraced` hold
that flat `Traced` and take the user's non-static arguments as flat leaves. The
wrapper closures around the user's rules hold a FlatTree of the arguments
(nondiff arguments as `FTStatic`s, key paths as leaves), and use it and the
original `Traced`'s output tree to rebuild user pytrees only at the rule
boundary, after instantiating (or converting to `SymbolicZero`) any internal
symbolic zeros. Residuals cross the `HiPrim` boundary as
`(leaves, Static(treedef))`.

Validating pytree nodes still can't hold leaves that the user-facing API itself
makes non-Arrays: symbolic zeros under `symbolic_zeros=True` (`SymbolicZero`,
`CustomVJPPrimal`), and accumulators under `defvjp_with_accums`.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Improve accuracy of real gamma and factorial.

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy of real gamma and factorial.

Real `jax.scipy.special.gamma` previously used a single-word Lanczos approximation (~10 ULP error on CPU/GPU and ~300 ULP on TPU), and `jax.scipy.special.factorial` evaluated `exp(lgamma(n + 1))`, losing precision on larger integers.

Implement real `gamma` in `jax._src.scipy.gamma` using `(hi, lo)` double-word arithmetic with shared `exp_f2_mant_exp` and `scale_f2_pow2` helpers in `jax._src.lax.double_word`, and route `factorial(n)` through `gamma(n + 1)`. Real `gamma` now stays within 0.5 ULP for `bfloat16` and 1.0 ULP for `float16`, `float32`, and `float64` across CPU, GPU, and TPU, and returns exact factorials up to 34! in `float32` and 170! in `float64`.

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules).

head_commit.message:
Honor max_iterations and eps in jax.scipy.linalg.polar

polar(method="qdwh") silently ignored max_iterations, because _polar_2d
never passed it to qdwh. Passing any eps raised a ValueError: since
9fd5f7c6a, qdwh takes eps and max_iterations as static arguments, but
polar and _polar_2d traced them, so qdwh received a tracer and failed to
hash it.

Mark eps and max_iterations static in polar and _polar_2d, and forward
max_iterations to qdwh.
